result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers say plainly that the numbers show the course was delivered and well received, not that agents do the job better. A explicitly proposes a delayed scenario check and QA review of real tickets in weeks 3–6, keeps the plan lean, and warns against treating the prior-cohort comparison as proof. B states the n=12 and no-control-group limits more directly, but its metric list is longer, its suggestion of a concurrent control group leans toward a research study, and its director wording slightly overclaims ('agents are absorbing the content'). | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers say plainly that the current numbers don't show the program worked, and both give the director a usable script. B is better on later checks: it adds a scenario check a week or more after the course and has leads score real tickets in weeks 3–6. B also handles the small sample more carefully, calling any cohort comparison rough and suggesting counts instead of percentages. A's plan is broader than a small team needs, with a concurrent control group, retention tracking and a quiz-validity study.
